clue.text: Free school meal tiny? Rashford's first to get involved

parts.note: COMP is short for comprehensive, the standard British state secondary school

indicators.note: letters that get involved are mixed up together, so the fodder is rearranged
first here asks for only the opening letter of the footballer's name

explanation.surface: A nod to footballer Marcus Rashford's campaign for free school meals for children in need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school meal' reads as one phrase, but 'school' gives COMP alone. Marcus Rashford is an England footballer who campaigned for free school meals in 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complimentary is given without charge, like a complimentary ticket.

clue.text: Blur faces but nothing otherwise

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: An instruction for pixelating faces in a photo, or else blurring nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' shuffles FACES BUT plus O.
explanation.definitionFit: To obfuscate is to make something unclear or muddled, which is to blur it.

clue.text: Reduced clergyman's department finally

indicators.note: finally sends the letter for department to the very end of the word

parts.note: a padre is a clergyman, especially a military chaplain; the 's links him to the department

explanation.surface: A clergyman's department faces budget cuts in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' moves the D of PADRE to the end, giving PARED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pared means cut down or trimmed, as when costs are pared back.

clue.text: Set off crash dieting

indicators.note: crash suggests something smashed apart and in disarray, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crash diet sets off some health reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' looks like part of the phrase 'crash dieting', but it is the anagram signal for DIETING.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a fire or a fuse is to ignite it; both mean started burning.

clue.text: Excuses from sweetheart — and address for woman taking part

parts.note: ex is Latin for from or out of, as in ex officio
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: taking means holding something within, so the form of address wraps the part

parts.note: Ms is a form of address for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone's partner makes excuses to get out of attending a social event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover, but it is the heart of 'sweet'. 'taking' wraps the address for a woman around the part.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to excuse them from a duty or rule.

clue.text: Islanders unhappy deporting duke? Wait and see

indicators.note: unhappy suggests things in a bad way, so the remaining letters are jumbled
deporting means sending someone out, so the letter for duke leaves the phrase

explanation.surface: Unhappy islanders face a deportation decision and are told to wait and see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deporting' takes D out of WAIT AND SEE, and 'unhappy' shuffles the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taiwanese are the people of Taiwan, an island nation off China.

clue.text: Food that I arranged — not all of it turned up

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
not all of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A host complains that the guests did not touch all the food they had arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads ATIAR (from thAT I ARranged) upwards, which in a down clue means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian yoghurt side dish, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Enjoy one's job looking after Charlie — secure and trouble-free

indicators.note: looking after is read as placed after, so the job comes after Charlie and secure

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to lock something is to secure it
one's job is one's work

explanation.surface: Someone loves their job of minding a child called Charlie, which goes safely and smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking after' looks like childcare, but it means placed after Charlie and secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes like clockwork runs smoothly, with no hitches.

clue.text: Attempt to discredit press cameraman — pigs!

indicators.note: to press something is to squash it out of shape, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A smear campaign against a press photographer, dismissed as pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like the newspapers that a cameraman works for, but it is the anagram signal for CAMERAMAN PIGS.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear campaign spreads damaging claims to ruin someone's reputation.

clue.text: Isn't regularly on guard outside, one's deduced

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word
outside means the guard surrounds the word for on

parts.note: a fence is a guard or barrier
re means on or about, as in a letter's subject line

explanation.surface: Someone working out who isn't guarding a fence properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the odd letters of Isn't; 'outside' puts the guard around the word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: An inference is a conclusion one has reached by reasoning, which is what one has deduced.

clue.text: 'I shall go first!' — little bossy woman oppressing Vlad, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: shall go first says the letter I is put at the front of the answer
oppressing means bearing down on and holding, so the bossy woman wraps the setter

parts.note: DOM is short for dominatrix, a dominant woman
Vlad is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A setter jokes about being bossed around by a dominant woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oppressing' places DOM around I, the setter Vlad; 'shall go first' puts the other I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression or turn of phrase, a particular manner of speaking.

clue.text: Became less ragged after trim

indicators.note: after a trim the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Something became less ragged after a trim, like a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Became less ragged' reads as one phrase, but the definition is just 'Became less'; 'after trim' takes T from TEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain or pressure that eased has lessened or diminished.

clue.text: Number One hit about Scottish holiday spot — one providing haven for Paul originally

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for hit goes around the town

parts.note: to tan someone is to hit or thrash them

indicators.note: providing haven for means sheltering inside, so the letters wrap the initial

parts.note: Oban is a seaside resort town on the west coast of Scotland

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the name

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A chart-topping single about a Scottish resort that once gave shelter to Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the resort, with Paul's initial sheltered inside it ('providing haven for'), within the word for hit; the A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the most important person, the boss or number one.

clue.text: Left and got picked up

parts.note: to earn money is to get it

explanation.surface: Someone left and was collected by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like a lift being given, but it means acquired knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill or language is to learn it.

clue.text: Tricked! Root in middle of house of ill repute!

indicators.note: tricked suggests something fiddled with and reworked, so the letters are rearranged
middle of takes the letters of the word with its ends removed

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation about a con trick in a brothel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' gives OUS from hOUSe; 'Tricked' rearranges ROOT IN plus OUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notorious is famous for bad reasons, widely known and disreputable.

clue.text: Pussy keeps heading for cream? I'm not sure

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the infected word wraps the initial

parts.note: pussy here means full of pus, which is septic

indicators.note: heading for points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cat goes for the cream, and the owner doubts it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussy' is a cat in the picture but means full of pus here; 'keeps' puts the C from 'heading for cream' inside SEPTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is a doubter, someone who would say they are unconvinced.

clue.text: Managed to stop one director touching up another

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the word for managed sits inside the director

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director
ran means managed, as one runs a business

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: on means touching, as a book on a table

explanation.surface: One film director tries to stop another from touching up his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: another director besides Jacques Tati. 'up' reads the word for touching from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is an American film director, so he is another director besides Tati.

clue.text: Kicks up fuss about energy-saving tariffs

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: saving is read as keeping inside, so the tariffs hold the energy letter

parts.note: rates are tariffs or charges
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about energy-saving tariffs on their bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicks up fuss about' reads as one complaint, but 'about' gives C. In British slang to create is to make a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, someone who is creating is making a fuss or complaining loudly.

clue.text: So gutted, having killed American — getting put away

indicators.note: gutted means its insides are taken out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus
offed is American slang for killed

explanation.surface: Someone devastated after a killing in America is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' takes the middle I out of SIC, leaving SC. 'So gutted' and 'put away' suggest misery and prison, but put away means eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To put food away is to eat it greedily, which is to scoff it.

clue.text: Proposition earth mother prepared to embrace

indicators.note: to embrace means to hold inside, so the shuffled word wraps the earth letter
prepared means made ready or worked up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is an abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Mother earth is ready to embrace a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'earth mother' reads as one phrase, but 'earth' gives E; 'prepared' shuffles MOTHER and 'to embrace' wraps it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem is a statement in mathematics to be proved, a proposition.

clue.text: Maybe roofer eating dates is not a great catch!

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the roofer wraps the dates

parts.note: a tiler is an example of a roofer, hence maybe
D is an abbreviation for date, so two dates give two Ds

explanation.surface: A roofer who eats dates is dismissed as a poor romantic prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not a great catch' looks like a romantic put-down, but means a small fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiddler is a very small fish, so an angler would think little of catching one.

clue.text: County town near London, home to royalty

indicators.note: home to means housing within, so the town wraps the royal letters

parts.note: Watford is a town in Hertfordshire just north-west of London
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A description of a town near London where royalty live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County town' reads as one phrase, but 'County' alone is the definition. Watford is a commuter town north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterford is a county in the south-east of Ireland.

clue.text: Rate old Boris — and for Macron that's upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting means turning upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Boris Johnson was the British Prime Minister, the PM
et is French for and, the word the French president would use

explanation.surface: Emmanuel Macron finds Boris Johnson's behaviour upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns the whole string over, which in a down clue means reading it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or pace of something, its rate.

clue.text: Girl or boy, one's a bit of alright

parts.note: a son is a boy
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's means is, linking to the next piece

indicators.note: a bit of points to just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Whether a girl or a boy, someone is attractive, a bit of all right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of alright' is British slang for an attractive person, but here 'a bit of' gives the A of alright.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonia is a female first name, so the definition works by example: a girl.

clue.text: Children about to pick up a small furry creature

indicators.note: to pick up is read as taking in, so the reversed word holds the A
about means turned round, so the word for children is read backwards

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: Children are about to pick up a small furry animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TOTS into STOT, and 'to pick up' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoat is a small weasel-like mammal with brown fur.

clue.text: Bounder stealing note, one for the ladies

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the bounder holds the note

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, bounds along
me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bounder, a cad, steals a note and is a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' suggests an old-fashioned cad, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Romeo is a womaniser, after Shakespeare's romantic hero.

clue.text: Support post

definitions.meaning: a body of supporters or fans

explanation.surface: Support post.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a group of fans; following also means after, the Latin sense of post.

clue.text: Right-wing faction helping … for payment!

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the right-wing party
a side is a faction or party
a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: A right-wing faction helps out, but only if it is paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a consideration' is an idiom meaning for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A consideration is a fee or reward, as in 'for a small consideration'.
